Headline: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell reports the Chiefs view Kenneth Walker as a potential three-down back.
News Snippet: What is clear in the wake of the Chiefs waiving Emari Demercado is that they don’t really have another player that qualifies as a passing-down back besides Walker without squinting. The other backs they kept are Emmett Johnson, a Day 3 rookie, and Brashard Smith, a gadget player without enough size to really block. Perhaps the Chiefs will address this in street free agency ahead of the season, but as things stand, it certainly seems like Walker will be involved on all three downs.

Headline: Lions placed RB Isiah Pacheco (back) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: It’s a familiar place for the 27-year-old running back. He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season. It sounds like former UFL star Jacob Saylors will enter Week 1 as the favorite for whatever portion of the carries Jahmyr Gibbs doesn’t take, not that it figures to be many.

Headline: Asked if he would play in Week 1 without a new contract, Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. said “I don’t know. I’ve got to talk to he guys upstairs (in the front office) and my agents about that one.”
News Snippet: We haven’t had much in the way of contract beefs this offseason, but Porter Jr. seems ready to make up for lost time here. The Steelers CB spent most of training camp on the active/PUP list with a “back injury.” It seems like there’s at least a real chance he skips out on Week 1 to prove a point if he isn’t paid.

Headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Broderick Jones will compete with Terence Steele for the starting right tackle job.
News Snippet: This is a bit surprising because the Cowboys had already had a competition for Tyler Guyton on the left side (that Guyton won), and it was assumed that Jones would come in and add to that competition. Not so fast. Steele just received a three-year contract this offseason and is on the books for a $15.2 million cap hit in 2027, so we’d be surprised if Jones won the job.

Headline: Cardinals placed TE Tip Reiman on the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season. Reiman went down with a gruesome leg injury in Week 5 against the Titans and was put in an air cast. Hunter Long, who the Cardinals acquired at last cuts, will likely fill in Reiman’s role early on this season.

Headline: Alvin Kamara (knee) is not practicing on Tuesday.
News Snippet: This isn’t a surprise, as Kamara’s timeline to return per Adam Schefter as of August 19 was a month away. What was a minor surprise is that Kamara wasn’t placed on injured reserve before the start of the season. Perhaps there is still a chance he can go in Week 1, though we’d call him doubtful at this point based on the initial timeline.

Headline: Eagles placed TE Grant Calcaterra on injured reserve.
News Snippet: It’s unknown what injury he has at this time. Calcaterra will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. It doesn’t seem like Eagles fans are particularly upset about this. Assuming they don’t bring in Zach Ertz as a secondary tight end, Johnny Mundt and Eli Stowers figure to be the main players behind Dallas Goedert this year.

Headline: Raiders placed EDGE Keyron Crawford on season-ending injured reserve.
News Snippet: The rookie third-round pick suffered a season-ending ankle injury in his final preseason game. Crawford will likely pick things back up next year with a chance to make real noise for the Raiders — and perhaps without Maxx Crosby in front of him — assuming no setbacks.

Headline: Jaguars placed OL Patrick Mekari (back) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Mekari, who underwent back surgery, will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. We’d bet on him missing more than four. Emmanuel Pregnon seems likely to start at left guard for the Jaguars as a rookie.

Headline: Saints signed WR Cedric Tillman to their practice squad.
News Snippet: In theory Tillman could put pressure on the back of the Saints wideout corps. In actuality, if they really thought that, they probably would have signed him to the active roster. Still, with only four healthy wideouts on the roster, Tillman could be elevated early. Zamir White is the other big name on the Saints practice squad and is joined by TE Stone Smartt, DE Fadil Diggs, RB CJ Donaldson, DB TJ Hall Jr., T Alan Herron, T Easton Kilty, WR Jalen Moreno-Cropper, WR Trey Palmer, LB Jackson Sirmon, K Charlie Smyth, DL Jay’Viar Suggs and T Alex Wollschlaeger

Headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Carnell Tate is “working out some stiffness” and did not practice on Tuesday.
News Snippet: This is, to be a broken record, probably not much to be concerned about just yet. The 21-year-old Tate is in a weird spot as a clear high-volume target on a passing offense that has not looked good all preseason and probably should be eyed skeptically heading into 2026. Nevertheless, Tate has the goods to be a fantasy producer this year if the offense around him is good enough to let that happen.

Headline: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) did not practice on Tuesday.
News Snippet: Neither did Ty Johnson (knee), with both players still having plenty of time to get back before next Sunday’s Week 1 game against the Texans. It’s hard to tell how seriously to take these because Joe Brady has been a brick wall on injury questions, but we’ll get a better indication next week when injury reports start to hit.

Headline: Bills placed Tyrell Shavers (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season after tearing his ACL in the playoffs. No surprise there. Shavers will likely be a late-season reinforcement, if that, in 2026 after coming on strong when the Bills needed receiving help last year.

Headline: Patriots placed EDGE Harold Landry on the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: The 30-year-old edge will miss at least the first four games of the season. He barely practiced this offseason and never got off the active/PUP list. It remains to be seen if Landry will get healthy enough to play this season.

Headline: Jets claimed K Blake Grupe off waivers from the Colts.
News Snippet: Jason Sanders, who had won the Jets kicker competition, is instead released to make way for Grupe. As we wrote about Sanders a few days ago: Winning the Jets kicker competition is not an endorsement that provides many fantasy points. Grupe will probably be stuck in the 20s in weekly ranks in most of the Jets games this year.

Headline: Steelers signed RB Lew Nichols to the practice squad.
News Snippet: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes Nicholes is the player he’d promote to join the carries split if either Jaylen Warren or Rico Dowdle is injured. Perhaps that’s enough of an endorsement to get him on the deep dynasty radar. RB Travis Homer, DB Doneiko Slaughter, WR Brandon Smith, WR Max Hurleman, OL Doug Nester, OL Steven Jones, DL Esezi Otomewo, DL Kyler Baugh, DB Sebastian Castro, LB Jacoby Windmon, TE Lake McRee and DE Julius Welschof were also signed to the practice squad.

Headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes Omar Cooper Jr.'s role “should grow over time.”
News Snippet: Cooper “started to show some signs of life by the end” of training camp. The first-rounder will split time with Isaiah Williams in the slot and also operate “as a gadget player.” Keep him out of lineups early, but he is still on the dynasty radar and should be monitored on the waiver wire in shallow leagues.

Headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Ja’Marr Chase (knee) will be “limited this week” but that he “feels good about his progress.”
News Snippet: We’re not viewing this as a major cause for concern, the Bengals have no reason to rush Chase back on the field after he hyperextended his knee last week. If he’s still drawing limited tags on the official injury reports next week, then we can start Panic Mode. Taylor added that Higgins (head contusion) may also be limited this week. "(Tee) and Ja’Marr will be good at the end of the week,” said Taylor.

Headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Tank Dell (knee) is “close” but “not quite there.”
News Snippet: He was already placed on injured reserve, so he’ll miss the first four games of the season. Reading between the lines it sounds like Dell has a chance to miss more than just the first four games of the season. Kayshon Boutte and Dalton Schultz will battle for the role of lead secondary target behind Nico Collins while Dell is sidelined.

Headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said there were “productive talks” on a contract extension for QB C.J. Stroud and that if a deal isn’t done before the start of the season, they’ll pick it up next offseason.
News Snippet: There’s really no reason for Stroud to want to negotiate off last year’s end-of-season performance, so we’re not stunned that there’s been no extension. It does sound like the Texans are at least laying the groundwork for next offseason. The general NFL expectation has been that Stroud will go into the year without an extension. The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan Alexander reported that league sources believe the Texans and Stroud’s camp “are not far off on what they think Stroud’s contract terms should look like and how much he should be paid per year.”

Headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Keylan Rutledge would start at left guard.
News Snippet: He called him “their best offensive lineman.” The big news here is that free-agent addition Wyatt Teller will start on the bench with Evan Brown starting at center. We’ll see if the Texans have finally hit on a formula that will help them run the ball, but it’s not great news for Teller that even the Texans don’t want to start him.

Headline: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said WR Savion Williams (ankle/IR) has a high-ankle sprain.
News Snippet: Williams was placed on IR at last cuts without an explanation of the injury, so here it is. Gutekunst said he thinks Williams will be ready when the four-week mandatory stay on IR is over.

Headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said the team traded for Kyle McCord to be the team’s No. 2 quarterback, but that he expects recently-claimed Brady Cook to “make a push.”
News Snippet: Riveting situation. The main fantasy takeaway here is probably something like “if Malik Willis gets hurt this year, all Dolphins pass-catchers will take major downgrades.”

Headline: Browns signed CB Noah Igbinoghene.
News Snippet: Igbinoghene didn’t survive last cuts with the Commanders, but catches on as a depth add in Cleveland. The 2020 first-rounder is entering his age-27 season. The Browns waived Michael Coats Jr. in a corresponding move.

Headline: Texans signed TE Brevin Jordan.
News Snippet: He was released at last cuts, but comes back as the Texans created extra roster space with a few injured reserve placements. DL Dominique Robinson also re-signed with the team.

Headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said the team has placed RT Braden Smith (foot) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Smith and OL Sam Hagen (undisclosed) will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season. The 30-year-old Smith was a priority free agent target for the Texans. Trent Brown will likely draw the starting nod at right tackle.

Headline: Lions signed TE Tyler Conklin.
News Snippet: They released him on Sunday, but it was merely roster manipulation as vested veterans aren’t subject to waivers. The 31-year-old should play a role as one of Detroit’s lower-end tight ends behind Sam LaPorta.

Headline: Browns signed EDGE Sam Williams to a one-year contract.
News Snippet: Williams was let go by the Cowboys at last cuts. He’ll become a part of a new-look EDGE room built around Jared Verse in Cleveland. Williams managed just one sack and six additional tackles for loss in 474 snaps with the Cowboys last year.

Headline: Emeka Egbuka (toe) did not practice on Tuesday.
News Snippet: Egbuka was given a ringing “hopefully” response from Todd Bowles when asked if he’d play in Week 1. We’re not overly concerned just yet, but he’s going to need to practice at some point to play. Jalen McMillan (knee) also sat, though we’re not as concerned about him since he’s practiced on that knee injury.

Headline: Colts GM Chris Ballard said Keenan Allen will play in Indianapolis’ Week 1 game against the Ravens.
News Snippet: In other words, there will be no in-house punishment for Allen being arrested for DWI and DWI endangering a person on Sunday morning. It’s a hard-to-augur game, as we are not entirely sure if the Ravens defense is going to take a turn for the better and if Daniel Jones is NFL-healthy rather than training-camp-healthy, but Allen should have enough of a role to land in the WR4 ranks at the very least.

Headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) returned to practice on Tuesday.
News Snippet: He missed about a week with the ailment, and reporters discovered that the “lower body injury” was a groin injury. We wouldn’t be surprised if he were limited a bit over the next two weeks, but if he’s practicing he’s certainly likely to play in Week 1.

Headline: Jonathon Brooks worked to the side of practice on Tuesday.
News Snippet: We’re not sure what Brooks is dealing with but his practice status will be something to monitor in the coming days. Chuba Hubbard, meanwhile, is practicing in full after missing weeks with a hamstring issue. Brooks headed into 2026 with a chance to be the Panthers’ lead back after fighting back through a series of catastrophic injuries. Carolina’s backfield could prove frustrating for fantasy purposes this season.

Headline: Colts general manager Chris Ballard said he expects Anthony Richardson, Jr. to remain with the team in 2026.
News Snippet: Richardson is listed alongside Riley Leonard as the team’s QB2 for now. Either Leonard or Richardson — who struggled in the preseason — will serve as Daniel Jones’ backup this season. One of the most inaccurate passers in modern NFL history, Richardson would be a massive downgrade for all Indy pass catchers if he finds his way under center in 2026.

Headline: 49ers general manager John Lynch said he hopes Mike Evans (adductor) will practice next week.
News Snippet: Evans’ Week 1 status is starting to look iffy after missing most of the past few weeks with various injuries. Entering his age-33 season, Evans will need to log at least a couple practices next week if he’s going to suit up against the Rams in the season opener. Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans is “ahead of schedule doing good. But we know with Mike and where he is at in his career, we’ll definitely have to treat him differently.” An Evans absence would be a marked boost for De’Zhaun Stribling and perhaps Deebo Samuel. Evans will be a name to watch in the coming days.

Headline: Tyler Warren (groin) practiced Tuesday.
News Snippet: Warren is recovering from an apparently minor groin injury. By all accounts he should be a full go for Week 1. Warren last season was top three among tight ends in targets per route run and first-read target rate in the balanced Colts offense. He’ll offer a sturdy weekly floor and could lead the team in targets in 2026 if he stays healthy.

Headline: Alec Pierce (ankle) practiced Tuesday.
News Snippet: Pierce missed most of training camp while recovering from offseason ankle surgery after signing a huge contract extension with the Colts. Pierce appears on track to suit up for Week 1. Whether Pierce is on some sort of pitch count remains to be seen. Pierce should eventually function as the team’s WR1, operating as more than a strictly downfield threat. He should be seen as a flex play for now.

Headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) was not seen at practice Tuesday.
News Snippet: Jeanty remains sidelined ahead of the Raiders’ Week 1 matchup against the Dolphins after sustaining a potentially high ankle sprain last week. Meanwhile, rookie RB Mike Washington “has changed the staff’s perspective of the running back room,” according to ESPN’s Ryan McFadden with some impressive play during training camp and in the preseason. Head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s “not making any promises on percentages of play time” for Washington or Jeanty ahead of the season opener. Jeanty could be a while before he’s ready to take on a true workhorse role in the Vegas backfield. Washington should be rostered in all fantasy formats for now.

Headline: Bucs general manager Jason Licht said there are no immediate plans to re-open contract talks with Baker Mayfield.
News Snippet: Licht during a Wednesday presser said the Bucs were “on to Cincinnati” with the regular season less than two weeks away. Licht has called Mayfield a franchise quarterback, but has not offered the veteran a long-term deal ahead of the 2026 season. Mayfield could be on his way out of Tampa in 2027 unless the team decides to use the franchise tag on him. Mayfield ranks 11th out of 40 qualifying QBs in adjusted EPA per drop back since the start of the 2024 season, ahead of Jalen Hurts and Dak Prescott, among others.

Headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected TE Luke Musgrave (neck) to play at some point in 2026.
News Snippet: Musgrave is coming back from a neck injury with no clear timeline for a return to action. The Packers last week signed Jonnu Smith, who will play behind Tucker Kraft to start the regular season. Smith could be an interesting waiver add if Kraft — returning from a major knee injury — misses any time in 2026.

Headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
News Snippet: “Asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs, Gutekunst says he wants to let the process play out,” The Athletic’s Matt Schneidmann said. Jacobs on Sunday was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List while his legal situation plays out. Jacobs in May was arrested and booked on five charges, including felony strangulation. ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Monday that Jacobs’ time on the exempt list was, for now, indefinite, and hinged entirely on how his legal situation unfolds. If damning video evidence is released, Jacobs could miss most or all of the regular season. MarShawn Lloyd would start the year as Green Bay’s lead back and has a chance to be one of fantasy’s best running back values.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Cade Klubnik will be the team’s QB2 to start the regular season.
News Snippet: What this means is that Geno Smith has plenty of job security. Klubnik in the preseason completed 21 of 34, passes for 190 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception while taking four sacks. Klubnik would be a marked downgrade from Smith if the veteran misses time in 2026.

Headline: Ravens signed K Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
News Snippet: It’s an interesting move after Tyler Loop, the team’s Week 1 starter, struggled in training camp and during the preseason. The journeyman Moody was most recently cut by the Commanders and would only be activated to the 53-man roster if Loop’s struggles continue into the regular season. Last year with Washington, Moody went 10-for-11 while going 2-for-2 on distances of 50-plus yards.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Jeremiyah Love is “about 50/50" to play in Week 1 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Love is still working his way back from a preseason high ankle sprain, and has been spotted doing some light practice work in recent days. The Cardinals will “have to see how he progresses” before they decided whether to make the rookie back active for Week 1. If Love is out for the season opener, Tyler Allgeier could see a heavy workload, as James Conner (ankle) begins the season on injured reserve.

Headline: Steelers general manager Omar Khan said the team would not engage in contract negotiations during the regular season.
News Snippet: That could mean the team will have to hammer out a new deal with Joey Porter, Jr. before the season kicks off in less than two weeks. The Steelers recently activated Porter from the PUP list after he dealt with a supposed back injury in the offseason. Porter will most likely have to play out his rookie contract or hold out. He would be a big loss for the Pittsburgh defense.

Headline: Malik Nabers (knee) remains noncommittal about his Week 1 status.
News Snippet: Nabers told reporters Monday that he still needed to clear a few checkpoints before being ready to suit up for the season opener against Dallas. “Will it take some time? Who knows?” he said. “But I know for sure if I’m out there, I’m going to run some routes.” Some routes and movements, he added, feel better than others on surgically-repaired knee. Even so, ESPN’s Jordan Raanan said the “expectation is [Nabers] will be playing barring some sort of setback.” A target hog who’s explosive with the ball in his hands, Nabers profiles as a risky fantasy selection for now. His absence in the season opener would be a blow to Jaxson Dart’s outlook.

Headline: Rich Cimini of ESPN reports that the Jets will sign Bailey Zappe to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Zappe was unable to win the backup quarterback position — that’s going to rookie Cade Klubnik — but he’ll remain in the organization as the emergency signal-caller behind Geno Smith and Klubnik.

Headline: Bills signed WR Greg Dortch to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Dortch was unable to make the Lions and was a relatively-surprising cut Sunday. The former Arizona wideout was a productive — albeit flawed — receiving option with the Cardinals, and it’s not hard to imagine him being someone who helps Josh Allen and the passing attack in Buffalo this fall. Fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach, but it’s at least someone to monitor.

Headline: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Blue was waived by the Cowboys and went unclaimed, and the 2025 fifth-round pick will remain in the NFC East. He’ll begin the campaign behind Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley as backups to Saquon Barkley, but some strong performances in practice could give the 22-year-old a chance to receive touches in 2026.

Headline: Buccaneers signed QB Easton Stick to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Stick was released by the Colts at the end of the preseason. He’ll be third on the depth chart to begin the year behind Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels.

Headline: Raiders placed WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. on the reserved/injured list.
News Snippet: Thornton has been dealing with an undisclosed injury that has prevented the wideout from practicing over the last month. The 23-year-old can return in four weeks, but there’s no timeline as to when the 2025 fourth-round pick will return to the Vegas lineup.

Headline: Chargers signed TE Patrick Herbert to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Herbert had initially chose to join the Jaguars squad after being a late cut by Jacksonville, but instead he’ll join his big brother Justin Herbert in Los Angeles. Nepotism doesn’t always have to be a bad thing.

Headline: Bears signed RB Salvon Ahmed to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Ahmed was one of the final cuts of camp, but the 27-year-old will provide an extra body for the Bears and could be active on gamedays depending on the health of the tailbacks ahead of the other Chicago options.

Headline: Myles Garrett (knee) did not participate in Monday’s practice.
News Snippet: Garrett continues to not practice while experiencing swelling in his knee. It sounds like this is more maintenance than anything else, as the Rams want the start pass-rusher to be ready to roll and at his best for the opener against the 49ers next week in Australia. Still, it’s something to keep an eye on.

Headline: Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell (undisclosed) did not practice Monday.
News Snippet: Mitchell has been out of action for more than a week after experiencing a “minor setback” for an undisclosed injury. This could be a situation where we’re all left in the dark until the team is required to disclose injuries in the week leading up to Week 1, leaving fantasy managers to plan for contingencies. Any missed time from Mitchell would be a measurable boost to the weekly expectations of Omarion Hampton.

Headline: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said RB Jeremiyah Love is “progressing really well toward playing in Week 1.”
News Snippet: Speaking to media Monday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said running back Jeremiyah Love “took another step yesterday and he’ll take another step today,” with the goal of being ready for Week 1, when the Cardinals visit the Chargers to kick off the regular season. The high ankle sprain suffered in the team’s first preseason game has the potential to cost Love regular season games considering the timing, but it sounds as if there is at least a sliver of hope that Love will not miss any regular season time. That said, there is also the possibility that Love is active come Week 1 but not at full strength, something that could realistically influence his workload early in the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor the situation closely as the regular season approaches.

Headline: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (lower body) did not practice Monday.
News Snippet: Flowers has been a bit banged up in the latter portions of the offseason program, missing practices for two separate issues over the previous month. Even so, the team continues to assert he will be fine for Week 1. Fantasy managers will want to track his status over the coming two weeks.

Headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports Steelers WRs DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman are “expected to be ready” for Week 1.
News Snippet: This was always though to be the case, with the team’s decision to keep only six receivers through cuts Sunday seemingly backing that notion up. Pryor adds that the teams is expected to “ease in” both Metcalf and Pittman, but it certainly sounds as if each receiver will be on the field in less than two weeks for Week 1.

Headline: Former Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue goes unclaimed on waivers.
News Snippet: Blue now becomes a free agent and can be signed by any running back-needy team, including the ability to sign onto the Dallas practice squad. It has been quite the fall from grace for Blue over the previous 24 hours, seemingly going from the favorite for backup duties for the Cowboys to without a home. It is also noteworthy that only one running back was claimed during the waiver period, veteran Emari Demercado, by this same Cowboys team. Blue appears to have lost all fantasy value and faces an uphill battle for a meaningful role in his sophomore campaign.

Headline: Browns WR Isaiah Bond cleared concussion protocol.
News Snippet: Even so, the team was uncertain whether he would take part in practice Monday. Bond likely finds himself competing with veteran Jerry Jeudy for perimeter snaps at wide receiver for the Browns after the team’s release of Cedric Tillman over the weekend.

Headline: Raiders claimed CB Darrell Luter via waivers.
News Snippet: The Raiders had the No. 1 waiver spot and used it to claim just one player, cornerback Darrell Luter, who was released by the 49ers Sunday. Luter is likely to join the active roster for a team in desperate need of depth pieces in the secondary.

Headline: Dolphins claimed QB Brady Cook off waivers from the Jets.
News Snippet: Cook joins starter Malik Willis and recent acquisition Kyle McCord in the pecking order at quarterback for the Dolphins, with the assumption that McCord will serve as the primary backup on game days during the regular season. Either way, Cook now gets a fresh start after four starts across five appearances for the Jets during his rookie season. Tight end Justin Joly also joins the Dolphins after being released by the Broncos. The team kept four tight ends through final cuts, making the path to a roster spot more muddied, but he lands on his feet after being forced to contemplate a potential practice squad spot in Denver. Also claimed were DB Marcellus Dial, T Chukwuebuka Godrick, T Jarrett Kingston, DB Reese Taylor, and DB Julius Wood.

Headline: Cowboys claimed RB Emari Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Demercado enters a wide open backfield depth chart behind starter Javonte Williams and primary backup Malik Davis, the two of whom were the only running backs to survive 53-man roster cuts Sunday. It does not appear the Cowboys are finished adding to their backfield, with most teams keeping four running backs on the active roster throughout the season. More to come.

Headline: Eagles beat writer EJ Smith reports a reunion with TE Zach Ertz (knee) is on the table.
News Snippet: Ertz is on the mend after tearing his ACL last year. While nothing is imminent, Ertz could make sense for the Eagles current tight end room. Philadelphia is lacking in legitimate receiving options behind Dallas Goedart despite keeping four tight ends on their initial 53-man roster. Ertz turns 36 in November and is unlikely to be a fantasy factor at this point in his career, but could still be an upgrade on the Eagles’ current tight end depth.

Headline: Eagles signed RB Dameon Pierce to the practice squad.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Pierce was released by the Eagles on Sunday with the team keeping Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley to backup Saquon Barkley. Pierce will head to the practice squad and be the next running back up if an injury arises.

Headline: ESPN’s Brady Henderson believes the Seahawks will “roll with [Jadarian] Price as their lead back while mixing in a heavy dose of George Holani.”
News Snippet: Though Price did not play a single preseason snap and has missed time over the past few weeks with muscle soreness, he is widely expected to function as Seattle’s lead back in Week 1 against the Patriots, with Zach Charbonnet (knee) on the PUP list to begin the regular season. Holani, however, should see significant usage in the Seahawks backfield. His “receiving and pass-blocking skills seem perfectly suited for third-down work,” Henderson said. Emanuel Wilson, Henderson added, will be the “power complement to those two” if he’s fully recovered from an undisclosed injury. “Whatever plan Seattle has going into Week 1 will start to change once Charbonnet returns,” Henderson said. “Whenever Charbonnet is all the way back, it’s easy to envision the Seahawks splitting the work in their backfield fairly evenly between him and Price the way they did last season with Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III.” Sam Darnold has called Price a “special player” who excels as a pass catcher. For now it appears he’ll be an early-down option for Seattle’s offense.

Headline: Ravens released WR Chris Moore.
News Snippet: The Ravens aslso waived/released LB Michael Barrett, G Evan Beerntsen, DL Rayshaun Benny, WR Cortez Braham, C Corey Bullock, OL Gerad Lichtenhan, C Nick Dawkins, ILB Dominic DeLuca, DT Aaron Graves, WR Xavier Guillory, OLB Adisa Isaac, WR Cornelius Johnson, LB Jamon Johnson, LB Carl Jones, CB Robert Longerbeam, RB Dontae McMillan, DT David Olajiga, TE Ty Pezza, QB Austin Reed, CB Marquise Robinson, LB Kaimon Rucker, FB Lucas Scott, WR Octavian Smith, RB Elijah Tau-Toliver, WR Dayton Wade, S Silas Walters, CB Lardarius Webb Jr., LB Dion Wilson Jr., CB Amani Oruwariye, OT David Sharpe, S K’Von Wallace and RB Jonathan Ward.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the NFL has granted a two-game roster exemption for Rams DT Aaron Donald.
News Snippet: The exemption timeline is a little strange. Per Pelissero, it expires on September 11th, one day after the Rams’ Week 1 game against the 49ers. Regardless, it helps the team save roster space since Donald was officially reinstated to the active roster today.

Headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
News Snippet: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

Headline: Ravens placed Adam Randall on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Cornerback Bilhal Kone was also placed on IR. Both players can return after four games. Randall was likely parked behind Justice Hill as the Ravens’ RB3 heading into the season. That role now belongs to Rasheen Ali, at least until Randall is back in action. He played in the team’s final preseason game and the team has not said what this injury is yet.

Headline: Buccaneers waived WR Garrett Greene.
News Snippet: The Buccaneers also waived QB Connor Bazelak, OLB Chris Braswell, LB John Bullock, TE Devin Culp, TE Kenny Fletcher Jr., OT Marshall Foerner, DL Josiah Green, WR Matthew Henry, OLB Yasir Holmes, OG Nash Hutmacher, WR Jha’Quan Jackson, LB Nick Jackson, DL Jayson Jones, G Elijah Klein, RB Barika Kpeenu, OG Henry Lutovsky, S Robert McDaniel, CB Roman Parodie, WR Dean Patterson IV, K B.T. Headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (psoas) returned to practice Sunday.
News Snippet: Nacua had been dealing with psoas soreness in August, working off to the side or missing Rams practices for most of the month. He returns to practice Sunday and should not be in danger of missing any regular season time due to the injury. With news that Nacua will avoid the commissioner’s exempt list, he is still a good bet to go in the middle of the first round in fantasy drafts.

Headline: Saints placed RB Devin Neal on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, ending his season.
News Snippet: Neal has hit I.R. without a return designation, so his sophomore season is over. Of course, he could later be released with an injury settlement. The 2025 sixth-rounder managed 74 touches for the Saints’ undermanned 2025 running back group, though he was not impressive in the process. He is still only 23 years old, so he could land on someone else’s practice squad if/when the Saints cut him loose.

Headline: Seahawks placed Zach Charbonnet (knee) on the PUP list.
News Snippet: After months of Seahawks front office officials and coaches saying Charbonnet could be active for Week 1 against the Patriots, he’ll miss at least the first four games of the regular season as he recovers from his 2025 ACL tear. That leaves rookie RB Jadarian Price as the likely lead back to start the season, with George Holani perhaps functioning as the backfield’s pass-catching option and potential goal line back. Price, who missed time with lower body injuries in August, should be a full go for Week 1. He should be treated as a flex option to start the year.

Headline: Seahawks released CB Trevon Diggs.
News Snippet: Diggs, who doesn’t have an interception since the 2024 season, will likely latch on with another secondary in need of depth pieces. Diggs never had much of a chance of making the roster in Seattle, a defense sporting one of the league’s best coverage units. He totaled 31 pass breakups and 17 interceptions in his first three NFL seasons, from 2020-22. He’s totaled just six pass breakups and three interceptions since then. Diggs is entering his age-28 season.

Headline: Saints placed Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Tyson has been dealing with hamstring issues since his senior season at Arizona State. The issue flared up during training camp and he is now expected to be sidelined for roughly two months, as of two weeks ago. With an international game in Week 7 and a bye the following week, a Week 9 return looks like the most likely outcome for the rookie. He could still put up strong fantasy numbers in the second half of the season, but it’s hard to justify holding him in leagues with shallow benches.

Headline: Steelers activated Joey Porter Jr. (back) from the active/PUP list.
News Snippet: Porter Jr. spent all of training camp on the PUP list with a back issue. He was also searching for a new contract without much luck, so it’s safe to assume the back and bank issues were related. Without much leverage in the situation, he is likely stuck playing out the 2026 season on his rookie deal.

Headline: Cardinals placed James Conner on injured reserve.

Tight end Justin Joly also joins the Dolphins after being released by the Broncos. He will miss at least the first four games of the season and should remain on waivers.

Headline: Colts waived Blake Freeland.
News Snippet: Indy drafted Freeland in the fourth round of the 2023 draft. He made nine starts as a rookie but only took the field for 23 offensive snaps in his second season. Freeland then missed the entirety of 2025 with a fracture in his right leg.

Headline: Giants released OL Evan Neal.
News Snippet: Neal was somewhat inexplicably given a one-year contract in early March after one of the more disastrous rookie contracts in recent memory, only to be released during final cuts. Perhaps the team thought the magnetic polarities of the Earth would swap between then and now. Even so, the veteran minimum contract extended to the former first-round pick doesn’t cut too deep. He’s only 25, so perhaps an offensive line-needy team will try their hand at a career resurgence, but we wouldn’t count on it.

Headline: 49ers released WR KhaDarel Hodge.
News Snippet: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows said Hodge is a “strong candidate” to land on the Niners’ practice squad headed into the regular season. A journyeman wideout who plays special teams, Hodge most recently played four seasons with the Falcons, never recording more than 14 receptions over that span. He could find his way onto the 49ers active roster if the team suffers more receiver injuries this year.

Headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph will begin the season on the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: Joseph is still nursing a knee injury that hampered him last season. He will remain on the PUP list to open the season, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games.

Headline: Steelers kept all four quarterbacks for the team’s initial 53-man roster.
News Snippet: The Steelers will head into the regular season with Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar, who shined in training camp and during preseason outings in Mike McCarthy’s offense. If the 2026 season goes south for Pittsburgh, look for McCarthy to see what he has in Allar and perhaps Howard. Rudolph will likely back up Rodgers to start the regular season.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports J.J. McCarthy has made the Vikings’ initial 53-man roster.
News Snippet: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis made a Saturday stir when he left McCarthy off his Vikings 53-man roster prediction, but that would have been hasty even if the Vikes are convinced “Nine” has no future with the organization. This keeps open the possibility of some sort of pick swap trade, or perhaps even “development” behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. We doubt coach Kevin O’Connell is holding his breath on that one. A manifest bust through his first two years in the league, McCarthy could also end up waived later this week after the Vikes make a few waiver claims. Even if his time in Minnesota has yet to come to an end, the clock is still ticking.

Headline: Panthers placed RB Travis Etienne on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Etienne will be eligible to come off IR at some point during the 2026 regular season. He got some buzz during offseason workouts and training camp but has exceedingly little chance of seeing significant regular season snaps for Carolina. Etienne as a rookie in 2025 had 20 carries for 94 scoreless yards, functioning mostly as a kick returner.

Headline: Panthers acquired TeRah Edwards from the Chargers.
News Snippet: The Chargers’ compensation for the move hasn’t been announced, but it’s certainly a Day Three pick swap. Edwards went undrafted last year and signed with the Chargers’ practice squad. He did not play in 2025. To be honest, we’re not really sure what the Panthers are doing here.

Headline: Vikings waived Jermar Jefferson with an injury designation.
News Snippet: Assuming Jefferson clears waivers, he will revert to the Vikings’ injured reserve list and likely be cut with an injury settlement. The Vikings also waived/released CB Da’Veawn Armstead, WR Michael Briscoe, G Henry Byrd, WR Terrill Davis, C Gavin Gerhardt, G Joshua Gray, S Kahlef Hailassie, CB Tre Hawkins, LB Bangally Kamara, TE Marshall Lang, TE Matt Lauter, G Vershon Lee, OL Tristan Leigh, OL Delby Lemieux, CB Bryce Phillips, OL Tomas Rimac, DL Jahvaree Ritzie, LB Josh Ross, WR Trayvon Rudolph, WR Marcus Sanders Jr., RB Zavier Scott, OLB Cam’Ron Stewart, DL Smith Vilbert, CB Jarod Washington, CB Marcus Allen, OLB Kenny Dyson Jr., WR Dontae Fleming, TE Bryson Nesbit, LB Jacob Roberts, DL Jonathan Harris, P Johnny Hekker, DL Isaiahh Loudermilk, and S Tavierre Thomas.

Headline: Giants released OL Evan Neal.
News Snippet: Seriously, obviously. Neal was somewhat inexplicably given a one-year contract in early March after one of the more disastrous rookie contracts in recent memory, only to be released during final cuts. Perhaps the team thought the magnetic polarities of the Earth would swap between then and now. Even so, the veteran minimum contract extended to the former first-round pick doesn’t cut too deep. Perhaps an offensive line-needy team will try their hand at a career resurgence, but we wouldn’t count on it.

Headline: Texans waived WR Lewis Bond.
News Snippet: The No. 204 overall pick of the draft out of Boston College, Bond generated hype during the offseason program before turning in a solid preseason. It’s a bit of a surprise the receiver-needy Texans are passing on stashing him on the 53-man roster, but they will undoubtedly hope he clears waivers and lands on the practice squad.

Headline: Buccaneers released EDGE Chris Braswell.
News Snippet: The 2024 second-round pick never fully caught on in Tampa and was buried on the depth chart, with the team’s selection of Reuben Bain in the first round effectively sealing his fate. Braswell is likely to draw interest in the open market and could catch on as a pass rush developmental depth piece in short order.

Headline: Saints placed Mason Tipton on the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: Tipton will now miss at least the first four games of the season while on the PUP list. He is still recovering from a groin issue that landed him on injured reserve late in the 2025 season. With Tipton and Jordyn Tyson sidelined for the start of the season, Devaughn Vele and potentially rookie Bryce Lance will round out the team’s starting receiver trio for Week 1.

Headline: Xavier Restrepo made the Titans’ initial 53-man roster.
News Snippet: An undrafted free agent out of Miami, Restrepo joined the Titans last season and had 41 yards on three catches over his two active games late in the regular season. Restrepo led the Titans with eight catches and 97 receiving yards this preseason and seemed to surprise Titans beat writers with his ability to get open during training camp. He’ll start the season near the bottom of the team’s depth chart.

Headline: Patriots acquired OT Walter Rouse from the Vikings.
News Snippet: Rouse had been reported as waived, but the Pats swooped in with a Day 3 pick swap to secure his services. One of the last men on a strong overall New England roster, Rouse will have his work cut out for him to remain on the 53-man roster rather than being sent to the practice squad.

Headline: Lions released WR Greg Dortch.
News Snippet: It’s something of a surprise considering Dortch was productive in limited opportunities as a member of the Cardinals from 2021 to 2025. Dortch had 66 receptions and six touchdowns over the past two seasons with Arizona, occassionally drawing a start when the team struggled with wideout injuries. Look for Dortch to catch on with another team in the coming days or weeks as receiver depth.

Headline: Giants waived WR Jalin Hyatt.
News Snippet: The big-play threat who wasn’t, Hyatt never made the transition from the University of Tennessee’s simplistic offense to the big leagues. He caught 23 passes as a 2023 third-round rookie, but saw that number fall to 13 combined over the past two years. Chaotic coaching and quarterback situations surely didn’t help, but the reality is Hyatt was a one-trick pony who struggled with said trick. Although he is still only 25 years old next month, Hyatt is unlikely to have teams lining up to a take a deep-ball flier. Also waived/released by the Giants were QB Brandon Allen, WR Braxton Berrios, TE Tanner Conner, DL Marlon Davidson, EDGE Khalid Kareem, S Raheem Layne, OL Evan Neal, OL Lucas Patrick, DL Josh Tupou, DL Anquin Barnes, DL Ben Barten, S Beau Brade, WR Dalen Cambre, FB Grant Finley, EDGE Trace Ford, WR Xavier Gipson, RB Eric Gray, OL Jarrod Gray, QB Jake Haener, OL Jake Kubas, LB Chandler Martin, LB Darius Muasau, EDGE Caleb Murphy, DL Zaach Pickens, OL Ryan Schernecke, S J.T. Woods, CB Art Green and K Ben Sauls.

Headline: Texans placed WR Tank Dell on injured reserve, designated to return.
News Snippet: The designation to return means that Dell is expected to contribute in some capacity this season, although he appears a ways off still. With Jaylin Noel still nursing an injury after experiencing a setback and Jayden Higgins lost for the season, recent acquisition Kayshon Boutte has all the runway to operate as the WR2 opposite Nico Collins to start the season. Xavier Hutchinson should also see an uptick in opportunities while tight end Dalton Schultz should see a significant boost in weekly volume.

Headline: 49ers placed Isaac Guerendo to the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: Guerendo, still recovering from a pec injury, will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season. This helps to clarify the Niners backfield situation headed into the season. Behind Christian McCaffrey will be some combination of Kaelon Black — who has drawn praise from coaches and QB Brock Purdy — and Jordan James, who missed most of training camp with a rib injury. Guerendo is a long way from playing time in the Niners offense.

Headline: Rams released WR Alex Bachman.
News Snippet: The 30-year-old receiver has made a name for himself on special teams and as a blocker. He’s caught five balls over the last two years for the Raiders. Also waived/released by the the Rams on a quiet day of last cuts are: S Nick Andersen, OL A.J. Acuri, OL Austin Blaske, P Jack Bouwmeester, OL Wyatt Bowles, RB Dean Connors, S Alex Cook, OLB Devean Deal, WR Tru Edwards, CB Nyzier Fourqurean, LB Tomon Fox, CB Steven Gilmore, CB Al’zillion Hamilton, OL Blake Hance, OL Bryce Henderson, LB Nikha Hill-Green, S Tanner Ingle, DB Alex Johnson, TE Rohan Jones, DT Tim Keenan III, DB Cam Lamplin, DT Jaxson Moi, OL Larrell Murchison, LB Elias Neal, DL Bill Norton, LB Darryl Peterson III, WR Brennan Presley, LB Monty Rice, DL Tyler Scott and S Nate Valcarcel.

Headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that WR Odell Beckham has officially made the Giants’ roster.
News Snippet: Beckham’s spot on the depth chart is unclear, but he is unlikely to warrant FLEX treatment this season. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is reportedly slated for WR2 duties, and both WR Darius Slayton and WR Darnell Mooney could play ahead of Beckham. This is more of a feel-good story than an actionable fantasy-related item.

Headline: Chargers waived Junior Colson.
News Snippet: Colson was a third-round pick in 2024. He appeared in 11 games with one start, totaling 29 combined tackles and one pass breakup. Colson missed his entire second season with a shoulder injury. Expect another team to take a flyer on him in the next few days because of his draft pedigree.

Headline: Titans released WR K.J. Osborn.
News Snippet: Osborn largely spent the 2025 season as a free agent, joining the Falcons’ practice squad late in the year. He last appeared in an NFL game in 2024, playing seven games for the Patriots after spending four years with the Vikings. The Titans decide to part ways with the veteran as they go with younger depth at the wide receiver spot.

Headline: Colts released K Blake Grupe.
News Snippet: Grupe, who had a “90% make rate in camp” per Mike Garafolo, has a chance to come aboard late and win a different kicking job. Spencer Shrader will kick for the Colts this year.

Headline: Commanders released Van Jefferson.
News Snippet: Jefferson was in the running for a rotational role this summer, but a handful of younger players ultimately passed him on the depth chart. Treylon Burks appears to be the team’s WR3 for Week 1 while Jaylin Lane, Luke McCaffrey, and Antonio Williams are all vying for the WR4 gig.

Headline: Browns placed QB Dillon Gabriel (back) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Reporting had the Browns set to keep four quarterbacks on their initial 53-man roster, but this makes a little more sense. Gabriel was not spotted throwing at practice today, and now we know why. We have no idea when he suffered the back injury, but he’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season. The team also announced the final roster cuts to get down to the final, 53-man roster. Waived or released were DT Travis Bell, RB Davon Booth, DT Elijah Chatman, G Kinsley Eguakun, DE Logan Fano, WR Luke Floriea, WR Gage Larvadain, T K.T. Leveston, RB Ahmani Marshall, P Wes Pahl, DT Tyreak Sapp, DE Khordae Sydnor, LB Edefuan Ulofoshio, S Zion Washington, LB Nathaniel Watson, and WR Kole Wilson.

Headline: 49ers acquired G/C Jarrett Patterson from the Texans.
News Snippet: Patterson had slowly been phased out of the Texans’ OL plans and winds up dealt away after the team spent multiple picks on interior linemen in last month’s draft. He’ll challenge for the backup center position with the 49ers. Patterson started 21 games in three years with the Texans, though it’s fair to admit that it wasn’t exactly good experience.

Headline: 49ers released G Rob Jones.
News Snippet: Jones is a former undrafted free agent, signing with the Dolphins out of college in 2021. He started 30-of-49 games for the Dolphins across four seasons but spent all of last season on injured reserve with the Cowboys. The 49ers signed him as interior offensive line depth and he got some run with the first-team offense before a calf strain slowed him down. Jones now re-enters the free agent pool.

Headline: Texans acquired OT Nathan Thomas from the Cowboys in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
News Snippet: A 2024 seventh-rounder, Thomas appeared in all 17 games for the Cowboys last season, making four starts. He was supposedly a camp contender for the Cowboys’ blindside gig, but ended up fighting for second-team right tackle status. He’s a body to throw at the Texans’ ever-present OL problems.

Headline: Giants waived RB Eric Gray.
News Snippet: The writing was on the wall for Gray pretty much all offseason after Brian Daboll, who helped draft him, was fired. Najee Harris coming in to training camp late was just insult to injury at that point. The 26-year-old was in the final year of his rookie contract and will look to catch on elsewhere.

Headline: Chargers waived DJ Uiagalelei.
News Snippet: Trey Lance will back up Justin Herbert. Uiagalelei was waived by the Chargers at roster cutdowns last year as well. He stuck on the team’s practice squad and signed a reserve/future deal this offseason. He has a shot at landing on LA’s practice squad once again.

Headline: Broncos waived LB Red Murdock.
News Snippet: Per 9NEWS’ Mike Klis, the Broncos will sign Murdock to their practice squad if he goes unclaimed on waivers. Murdock made a name for himself as a voluminous tackler and fumble-forcer at Buffalo, leading the MAC twice and the FBS once in the latter category.

Headline: Texans released WR Sterling Shepard.
News Snippet: He lasted just nine days with the team. Shepard was signed before the Kayshon Boutte trade and the Boutte trade can be looked at as the end of any real chance for him to make the team. Shepard’s free agency was fairly slow and at 33 years old it wouldn’t be surprising if he had to sign to a practice squad if he wanted to keep playing.

Headline: Texans released WR Zay Jones.
News Snippet: He didn’t sign until late August after rehabbing a torn Achilles in Week 10. JJones was an emergency signing for the Texans, but they followed up on it by trading for Kayshon Boutte. The Boutte deal made Jones’ path to a roster spot tenuous. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere.

Headline: Packers placed Micah Parsons (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
News Snippet: This move was expected. Parsons himself said a few weeks ago that a Week 6 return was his “most optimistic” timeline. A spot on the reserve PUP list means Parsons must miss at least the first four months of the season. He is still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in Week 15 of the 2025 season. Parsons should still be a force on the defensive front when he’s back, but that won’t happen until at least October.

Headline: Commanders released DT Shy Tuttle.
News Snippet: Tuttle began the 2025 season playing for the Titans and closed it playing for the Commanders, who released him today. He logged just 11 tackles and failed to pressure the opposing passer once.

Headline: Patriots released James Hudson.
News Snippet: The Pats signed Hudson to a one-year deal in the offseason. He appeared in 11 games for the Giants last year, making two starts. Hudson has 60 career appearances and 19 starts. He should be able to find a new home over the next week or two as rosters shake out.

Headline: Rams signed DT Aaron Donald to a one-year, $20 million contract.
News Snippet: The incentive-heavy deal is worth a maximum of $30 million for the longtime defensive stalwart, who comes out of a two-year retirement to chase another ring with the Rams. Donald worked out at the team facility multiple times throughout the offseason, making the signing less shocking than it otherwise would have been had there been no ties between the two sides earlier this summer. The Rams now carry one of the top defenses in the league after the acquisitions of Myles Garrett, Jaylen Watson, and Trent McDuffie this offseason, in addition to coming off a season in which they led the league in scoring at 30 points per game. The betting favorites to win the Super Bowl in February gain another weapon.

Headline: Giants released WR Braxton Berrios.
News Snippet: However, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports it’s a roster maneuver, and that special teams ace Berrios is expected to re-join the team before Week 1. We will take Schefter at his word.

Headline: Broncos waived TE Justin Joly.
News Snippet: 9NEWS’ Mike Klis writes that Joly “clearly” could use a redshirt year, which isn’t exactly great news for his dynasty prospects. We’ll see if another team wants to take a chance on him rather than letting him join Denver’s practice squad. Joly was a fifth-round pick this past year and it’s rare for teams to cut picks this early, but Denver’s roster is loaded.

Headline: Cowboys waived OG Trevor Keegan.
News Snippet: Keegan earned a 65.3 PFF run-blocking grade in one game with the Eagles in 2024. He played just six snaps on offense with the Cowboys last year.

Headline: Texans waived RB Noah Whittington.
News Snippet: Whittington is a 24-year-old undrafted free agent rookie. He will likely be given the chance to make a practice squad in Houston or elsewhere.

Headline: Commanders waived RB Robert Henry Jr.
News Snippet: Henry was a depth backup for the Commanders’ running back room after signing as an undrafted free agent out of UTSA. He had a solid preseason showing but the Commanders had little room on the main roster with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White, and Kaytron Allen ahead on the depth chart. Henry is a candidate to return on the practice squad.

Headline: Cowboys waived Michael Trigg.
News Snippet: Trigg went undrafted in the spring and signed with Dallas as a UDFA. He made some noise in camp but ultimately not enough to crack the 53-man roster. Trigg is a strong candidate to make it back on the team’s practice squad as a developmental tight end.

Headline: Cardinals waived LB Owen Pappoe.
News Snippet: Pappoe was a fifth-round pick by the Cardinals in 2023. He appeared in 49 games over three seasons for Arizona, primarily as a special-teamer. Pappoe tallied 27 combined tackles and two passes defended last season; he will look for another role as a reserve linebacker or special-teamer in 2026.

Headline: Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue.
News Snippet: Well this one is going to leave a mark. 2025 fifth-rounder Blue was a summer ’25 fantasy creation the Cowboys never seemed to get behind, confirming as much when they made him a Week 1 healthy scratch. That set the tone for a bitterly disappointing rookie year that featured just 39 touches. This offseason seemed to be different, however, with head coach Brian Schottenheimer spending the spring dishing out over-the-top positive quotes on his second-year back. The praise again died down during training camp, but Blue showed well in his preseason action. Just apparently nowhere close to well enough to beat out survivor veteran Malik Davis for No. 2 status behind Javonte Williams. Blue is still only 22 years old, but his back-to-back failures to earn pass-catching duties in a backfield that could really use such a player is an ominous sign for his NFL future. He’s now a tenuous hold in dynasty leagues despite his youth and past high expectations. All of that being said, it is possible once the cut-down dust settles that either Blue or fellow waived sophomore Phil Mafah end up back on the Cowboys’ 53-man roster.

Headline: Texans waived Jamal Hill.
News Snippet: A 2024 sixth-round pick, Hill has appeared in 20 games for the Texans over the past two years. He has only three defensive snaps to his name but has taken the field for 365 special teams reps. Hill’s special teams prowess could earn him a spot on Houston’s practice squad.

Headline: Broncos waived S Miles Scott.
News Snippet: The Broncos reportedly want to bring back the seventh-round rookie via the practice squad. They will be able to do so if he clears waivers.

Headline: Commanders released Trent Scott.
News Snippet: Scott has been with the Commanders for each of the past three seasons, appearing in 35 games with six starts, not including the postseason. He even caught Jayden Daniels’ first touchdown pass in 2024. Scott is a candidate to land on Washington’s practice squad.

Headline: Cardinals released OL Matt Pryor.
News Snippet: This is a tad surprising because the Cardinals needed help on the offensive line following OG Chase Bisontis’ knee injury, and Pryor has experience at OT and OG. Pryor could return via the practice squad.

Headline: Chargers released S Tony Jefferson.
News Snippet: The 34-year-old will likely be kept in some form — practice squad or re-signed after some shuffling at last cuts — and this will just be roster manipulation. The 34-year-old started eight games last year and played in 13 for the Chargers.

Headline: Commanders waived QB Sam Hartman.
News Snippet: Although he entered the league just two years ago, Hartman is already 27 years old. He has never seriously competed for the Commanders’ No. 2 job. He will likely head back to the practice squad, but the odds are getting longer Hartman ever makes a regular season appearance.

Headline: Seahawks acquired CB Avery Smith from the Chargers in exchange for a sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Tom Pelissero. It’s no secret that the Seahawks have been looking for cornerback depth this preseason. Seattle signed Trevon Diggs and Terrion Arnold in recent weeks. Now the Seahawks send out a sixth-round pick to bring in Smith, a UDFA from Toledo who was a standout in Chargers training camp.

Headline: Texans released S George Odum.
News Snippet: The former 49ers and Colts special teams star will not make the roster in Houston. Another team could give him a chance, though. He totaled four special teams tackles in three games last year.

Headline: Giants released QB Brandon Allen.
News Snippet: Allen backed up Cam Ward for the Titans last season, but was little more than a camp arm for the Giants behind Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston. About to turn 34 with just 97 attempts since the 2020 season, Allen is probably nearing the end of the NFL line.

Headline: ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi reports QB Taylen Green has made the Browns’ initial 53-man roster.
News Snippet: Cleveland is expected to keep all four of its quarterbacks for the 53-man roster. That includes Deshaun Watson, the team’s Week 1 starter, along with Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and Green, who was selected with the 182nd pick in the 2026 draft. The hyper-athletic Green could be used as a trick play option in Todd Monken’s offense. Green in 2025 led all college football players in EPA per rush.

Headline: Cowboys released Marquez Valdes-Scantling.
News Snippet: Valdes-Scantling signed a one-year deal with the Cowboys this offseason. He barely garnered more than the veteran minimum and was clearly nothing more than a depth option for the team. With well over 100 career games across six teams to his name, MVS should still find a team willing to carry him on their practice squad in the coming days.

Headline: Cardinals released CB Sean Murphy-Bunting.
News Snippet: Murphy-Bunting missed 2025 with a torn ACL. He missed a portion of training camp this month, but it is unclear why. He resumed practicing on August 17th. If healthy, he could compete for a backup role elsewhere.

Headline: Titans waived QB Will Levis.
News Snippet: An ill-fated “second-round savior” in the 2023 Draft, now 27-year-old Levis is sent packing from the Music City with 21 starts under his belt. That included zero in 2025 as Levis missed the entire season with a shoulder injury behind No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward. In theory, Levis “competed” for the backup job this summer, but journeyman free agent Mitch Trubisky was always the heavy favorite. Levis has all the physical talent in the world, but not the accuracy or processing, at least so far. It’s possible a more functional franchise could turn him in to a legit No. 2 quarterback, but that does not seem terribly likely at this point.

Headline: Giants released DT Zacch Pickens.
News Snippet: Pickens is a former third-round pick, appearing in games for the Bears and Chiefs since being drafted in 2023. The 26-year-old signed with the Giants this offseason and took some first-team reps in camp as the team tried several different things to solve their defensive tackle puzzle. Ultimately, the Giants decided Pickens is not a part of the equation for 2026.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Puka Nacua is expected to avoid the commissioner’s exempt list to begin the regular season.
News Snippet: Three players landed on what amounts to the “suspended with pay” list on Sunday, but Pelissero reports Nacua isn’t one of them. That does not necessarily mean Nacua is out of the woods for all time with the NFL, but his situation did not rise to the level of Josh Jacobs’ in the eyes of the shield. Now the main Week 1 question mark for Nacua is his groin injury, but it is not expected to keep him out of the Rams’ Australian opener vs. the 49ers.

Headline: Cowboys waived RB Phil Mafah.
News Snippet: Mafah became the off man out of the backfield rotation behind starter Javonte Williams Sunday, leaving Malik Davis and Jaydon Blue left to fight for primary backup duties. Blue appears to have an established change-of-pace role, making it more likely Davis operates in more of a pure handcuff fashion to begin the season.

Headline: Chiefs waived Esa Pole.
News Snippet: Pole signed with the Chiefs as a UDFA last year. He didn’t make their final roster and spent some time on the Jets’ practice squad before returning to the Chiefs late in the season. Pole went on to make four starts at left tackle late in the year and played reasonably well. His release is a bit of a surprise.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the NFL will place Broncos EDGE Jonathan Cooper on the commissioner’s exempt list.
News Snippet: Cooper is facing felony assault charges in addition to other chargers including domestic violence and harassment. The 28-year-old was slated to be Denver’s starting outside linebacker opposite Nik Bonitto, but now they’ll have to look at depth options while waiting for the commissioner to clear Cooper.

Headline: Falcons waived RB Nathan Carter.
News Snippet: Carter signed with the Falcons as an undrafted free agent last season, appearing in seven games for Atlanta. He carried the ball nine times for 60 yards and lost a fumble in 2025. With the emergence of Tyler Goodson as a viable depth option in the running back room, the Falcons jettison Carter heading into final cuts.

Headline: Packers acquired TE Mark Redman from the Rams in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round pick.
News Snippet: The Packers’ tight end room was a tad thin, so the move makes sense. They signed TE Jonnu Smith earlier this week. Redman is a second-year player who went undrafted in 2025.

Headline: Saints released RB Zamir White.
News Snippet: White, who had 12 carries over six games for the Raiders in 2025, won’t be on the Saints’ 53-player roster to start the season, leaving Audric Estime and Devin Neal as the team’s third and fourth backfield options, respectively. White could land in another backfield in need of depth in the coming weeks.

Headline: NFL placed Packers RB Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner Exempt List.
News Snippet: Jacobs was charged on two misdemeanors last week after initially being arrested in late May on five counts, including one felony. The NFL will now use the Commissioner Exempt List as they gather more information about the incident in question, which involved brutality towards a female in the garage of a shared home. Jacobs will still be paid but will be unable to participate in practice while he remains on the exempt list, although players are typically allowed to participate in team meetings. There is no telling how long Jacobs will remain on the exempt list as only the Commissioner holds the authority to remove him, meaning Jacobs could be away from the team until the criminal system is complete or he could be active in Week 1. Jacobs’ initial appearance in court is not scheduled until November, coinciding with Week 11, leaving a wide range of outcomes for fantasy managers to begin the season. Reports from the organization were far from forthcoming in recent weeks, most recently acquiring former Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson in a trade executed Sunday. Reading the tea leaves paints a morbid picture for Jacobs’ availability to start the 2026 regular season in less than two short weeks. MarShawn Lloyd suddenly finds himself atop the backfield depth chart in Green Bay and is a priority waiver addition for leagues that have already drafted, and should be treated as an upside back in the middle rounds of drafts.

Headline: Falcons released DE Cam Sample.
News Snippet: Sample began his career with the Bengals, spending the last five years in Cincinnati. He initially signed with the 49ers this offseason, then went to the Falcons after the 49ers waived him. Serving as a preseason rotational defensive lineman, the Falcons decide to part ways with Sample heading into final cuts.

Headline: Seahawks released S D’Anthony Bell.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Jordan Schultz. Bell was one of the more well-liked players in the Seahawks’ locker room, according to Schultz. He finished last season in Carolina after the Panthers claimed him off waivers towards the end of the regular season. Bell also contributes to special teams, which could make him a fit on the practice squad.

Headline: Falcons waived WR Vinny Anthony.
News Snippet: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes the Falcons will sign Anthony to the practice squad if he goes through waivers unclaimed. The team signed him as an undrafted free agent rookie earlier this year.

Headline: Eagles released RB Dameon Pierce.
News Snippet: Per Aaron Wilson, the Eagles want Pierce back on the practice squad. We’ll see how that goes. Pierce is a good returner so he does have some special-teams versatility.

Headline: Raiders released TE Albert Okwuegbunam.
News Snippet: Okwuegbunam was once a key part of the Broncos’ tight end rotation in 2021, but has only appeared in one game over the last two years. He caught five passes for 36 yards in a single game for the Raiders last season. Las Vegas now releases the 28-year-old as he looks for a new practice squad home for 2026.

Headline: Saints waived Charlie Smyth.
News Snippet: New Orleans signed Smyth to a three-year deal last December, so it’s a bit of a surprise to see him cut so soon. One of Tanner Brown or Daniel Carson will serve as the team’s kicker this season. An Irish native, Smyth joined the league as an International Pathway player, meaning the Saints can get a roster exemption for him if they choose to keep him on their practice squad.

Headline: Titans released RB D’Ernest Johnson.
News Snippet: Johnson, who has bounced around the league since spending his first four pro seasons with the Browns, will likely end up on another roster as a depth piece. Johnson has just 28 rushing attempts over his past three seasons with various teams, including the Patriots in 2025. It looks like Nicholas Singletary and Michael Carter will function as the Titans’ RB3 and RB4, respectively, behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears.

Headline: Bears released OT Jedrick Wills.
News Snippet: This is unfortunate. Wills spent 2025 rehabbing knee issues stemming from the 2023 season. The former PFWA All-Rookie Team (2020) member may be able to find a backup role elsewhere in the NFL. He left practice early last week and may have suffered an injury.

Headline: Jets acquired C Jordan Meredith from the Raiders.
News Snippet: The trade was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport, who added that the Jets and Raiders are “flopping” 2027 sixth- and seventh-round picks as part of the deal. Meredith started 19 games for the Raiders over the last two years and signed a one-year deal as a restricted free agent in the offseason. Now he’ll head to the Jets, where he’ll serve as much-needed interior offensive line depth.

Headline: Packers released Pierre Strong.
News Snippet: Strong was released right after it was reported that the team was acquiring Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers. He spent the 2025 season on the Packers’ practice squad and was elevated for two games. Strong will likely find work on another practice squad once rosters are settled.

Headline: Chiefs released CB Kaiir Elam.
News Snippet: The former first-round pick is back on the market. Elam spent time on the Cowboys’ and Titans’ rosters last year after a three-year stint with the Bills. He has decent odds of landing with another team at age 25.

Headline: Ravens waived EDGE Adisa Isaac.
News Snippet: Isaac, who missed all of last season with an elbow injury, was late to return to practice this offsseaon. He played 32 defensive snaps in 2024. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Isaac is “expected to draw interest” from teams.

Headline: Bears released Scotty Miller.
News Snippet: Miller signed with the Bears this offseason but failed to crack their 53-man roster as a depth option. With 93 career games under his belt and some experience on special teams, Miller should at least be able to land a practice squad gig in the coming days.

Headline: Commanders released OG Max Scharping.
News Snippet: Scharping was signed earlier this month. He has not played much in recent years and tore and ACL in September 2025.

Headline: Buccaneers agreed to terms with RB Sean Tucker on a one-year, $2.5 million contract.
News Snippet: The contract comes fully guaranteed as Tucker gets the stability he was looking for this offseason after entering 2026 on a restricted free agent tender of $3.52 million. Tucker presumably sits third on the depth chart at running back for the Buccaneers after the addition of Kenny Gainwell, a situation he has grown accustomed to during his time in Tampa. The pay cut likely stands as a boost to starter Bucky Irving after numerous reports this offseason called for a potential three-way timeshare in the backfield, something that now appears less likely given current circumstances.

Headline: Buccaneers waived OLB Jack Pyburn.
News Snippet: The undrafted free agent rookie led the NFL with four preseason sacks this year. He is a candidate to land on a practice squad somewhere, if not in Tampa Bay.

Headline: Rams released DT Larrell Murchison.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Aaron Wilson. Murchison was originally a fifth-round pick by the Titans in the 2020 NFL Draft. He appeared in 16 games with the Rams last year and had two sacks and three QB hits.

Headline: Commanders released OL Daniel Brunskill.
News Snippet: The seven-year veteran has amassed 71 starts across 108 appearances for the 49ers, Titans, and Dolphins and could quickly find his way onto an NFL roster as a viable depth piece capable of playing all five positions along the offensive line. He provides precisely the profile typically lauded by the Kyle Shanahan-Sean McVay coaching trees, which requires plus football IQ along with the ability to understand how multiple positions work together up front.

Headline: Bills waived WR Ja’Mori Maclin.
News Snippet: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that Maclin could return to Buffalo as a member of the practice squad. Maclin, former NFL WR Jeremy Maclin’s cousin, was an interesting preseason follow.

Headline: Bears released CB Terell Smith.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune. A fifth-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft by the Bears, Smith wasn’t a starter and managed just one interception and 10 passes defended in 26 games for Chicago over the last two years. The Bears traded for CB Clark Phillips early Sunday morning, which potentially made Smith expendable. He’ll hit the open market and could help a team in need of cornerback depth.

Headline: Commanders released RB Craig Reynolds.
News Snippet: Now on the wrong side of 30, Reynolds spent most of this decade as a lightly-used but valuable Lions reserve, at least in the eyes of the coaching staff. Washington was maybe the wrong place to try to latch on, as it had too much readymade NFL depth. Reynolds’ special teams expertise and reasonable amount of experience on offense could make him a stalwart of the 2026 workout circuit.

Headline: Bengals waived WR Mitch Tinsley.
News Snippet: Tinsley was a big hit last preseason and had an 8/116/2 receiving line last year in his age-26 season. He’s likely done enough to catch on someone’s practice squad, and perhaps has an outside chance of latching on to a 53-man roster. 2026 fourth-round pick Colbie Young will probably be the main outside backup, while Dohnte Meyers likely squeezed Tinsley out of a roster spot.

Headline: Bills released QB Shane Buechele.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Buechele, 28, has been a backup for years, spending time with the Chiefs and Bills. He was beat out by Kyle Allen, who will serve as the Bills’ QB2 this season.

Headline: Packers waived Domani Jackson.
News Snippet: Jackson was a sixth-round pick this year but failed to show enough in camp or the preseason to crack the team’s final roster. He also missed time during the offseason while recovering from core muscle surgery, hampering his development. He could return on the team’s practice squad if he clears waivers.

Headline: Bengals released QB Josh Johnson.
News Snippet: Johnson was signed before the Bengals knew they’d be getting Joe Flacco back, but with Flacco in the fold they’ve decided to move on from the 40-year-old. Johnson looked solid enough in the preseason to find a role elsewhere, hopefully on a team he hasn’t been on before for Immaculate Grid purposes.

Headline: Jaguars released QB Nick Mullens.
News Snippet: Bad backup quarterback play was a staple of camp reports for the Jaguars, so they dealt for Quinn Ewers yesterday and will now eat $3 million in guaranteed money to cut Mullens. Mullens will look to catch on elsewhere as the roster dust settles.

Headline: Dolphins acquired QB Kyle McCord from the Packers in exchange for a sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Packers is a 2028 sixth-round pick. After trading Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars, the Dolphins acquired their new backup QB in McCord, who had an impressive preseason. The Dolphins new GM and HC came from Green Bay this offseason and so did both of the quarterbacks on their active roster in McCord and starter Malik Willis. McCord was a sixth-round pick by the Eagles in the 2025 NFL Draft and is yet to appear in a regular season game.

Headline: Bucs waived Josh Williams.
News Snippet: Williams had a strong camp and even played ahead of Sean Tucker in a preseason game, causing some reporters to speculate that he could make the team’s 53-man roster over Tucker. While he likely earned himself a spot on the team’s practice squad if he clears waivers, Tucker remains the team’s RB3 heading into the season.

Headline: Panthers released QB Kyle Trask.
News Snippet: He’ll remain an emergency quarterback option for the team per Jeremy Fowler, which is a nice way of saying he’s not making the practice squad either. The 28-year-old former second-round pick will look for work elsewhere.

Headline: Dolphins waived Mark Gronowski.
News Snippet: Having already traded Quinn Ewers to Jacksonville, Miami only has Malik Willis on the roster at quarterback. They will make a move for a backup at some point in the next day or two. Gronowski is expected to return on Miami’s practice squad if he clears waivers.

Headline: Steleers released Dean Lowry.
News Snippet: Lowry appeared in a dozen games for the Steelers in 2024. He was a backup on Pittsburgh’s stacked defensive line and only recorded one sack. Lowry suffered a torn ACL and missed the 2025 season but still re-signed with Pittsburgh this offseason. At 32 years old coming off a torn ACL, Lowry may struggle to find a spot on a 53-man roster before Week 1.

Headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) hasn’t had any setbacks and is expected to practice this week, reports ESPN’s Adam Schefter.
News Snippet: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan caused some confusion earlier this week when he told reporters Kittle “took a step back.” Schefter cleared that up with his report Sunday morning that Kittle hasn’t had any setbacks in his recovery from a torn Achilles. According to Schefter, Kittle is expected to practice next week and still has a legitimate chance to play in Week 1’s game against the Rams in Australia. Fantasy managers could cover their bases by adding Jake Tonges in the event that Kittle isn’t active for the first game.

Headline: Jaguars waived QB Joey Aguilar.
News Snippet: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Aguilar joined the Jaguars in April as a UDFA from Tennessee, where he played one season. Aguilar turned 25 in June and is unlikely to be claimed by another team. Fowler adds that the Jaguars hope Aguilar returns to the practice squad, which seems like the most likely scenario.

Headline: Jaguars waived Yasir Abdullah.
News Snippet: Abdullah appeared in 10 games for the Jags last year but only logged two defensive snaps. He was on the field for 176 special teams snaps. He should be able to find a home on a practice squad once rosters are settled.

Headline: Cardinals acquired TE Hunter Long and a 2028 seventh-rounder from the Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-rounder.
